title: Staged rear-end collision with a pre-arranged lead vehicle
description: Investigators found that the 'victim' car braked sharply without reason on an empty city road so the insured vehicle would hit it from behind. Both drivers were relatives, the dashcam memory card was reported lost, and the same tow operator and garage appeared on three earlier rear-end claims within two months.

title: Repair invoice inflated by the workshop after approval
description: The approved estimate covered a bumper and one headlamp, but the final bill added a radiator, both airbags and an engine mount. Photographs showed the replaced parts were never damaged, the part numbers did not match the vehicle model, and the workshop owner was the claimant's brother-in-law.

title: Old dents and rust presented as fresh accident damage
description: A policyholder bought cover for a car that already had a crushed door and a cracked windscreen, then reported a hit-and-run a few weeks later. Photos taken at the pre-inspection, rust inside the dent and a resale listing from before the policy start date proved the damage existed beforehand.

title: Same incident claimed twice under two policies
description: One minor parking-lot scrape was reported to two different insurers within a week, each claim using a different date and slightly different photos of the same scratch. Matching chassis number, identical repair receipt serial and the same mobile number linked both submissions.

title: Phantom passengers added to a minor collision
description: After a low-speed bump, four injury claims were filed by people said to be riding in the car. Toll camera images showed only the driver in the vehicle, the passengers lived in another district, and all four were treated at the same small clinic by the same doctor on the same evening.

title: Vehicle reported stolen after being sold to a scrap dealer
description: The owner told police his SUV was taken from outside his house at night and claimed the full insured value. The vehicle had in fact been sold for cash to a scrap yard two days earlier; GPS tracker logs ended at the yard and the dealer's register listed the registration number.

title: Shop fire set deliberately to clear unsold stock and debt
description: A textile shop burned down overnight shortly after the owner increased the sum insured. Fire officers found accelerant traces at two separate starting points, the shutters had been left unlocked, and bank records showed heavy loan defaults and stock that had not sold for over a year.

title: Hospital admission and surgery that never took place
description: A health claim included discharge summaries, pharmacy bills and an operation note for a knee procedure. The hospital had no record of the patient, the surgeon named on the note was abroad on that date, and the bill format and stamp were copied from a different hospital's template.

title: Whiplash injury exaggerated for months of compensation
description: Following a gentle bump in slow traffic, the claimant reported severe neck and back pain, months of physiotherapy and loss of income. Social media posts during the same period showed him lifting weights and playing cricket, and the physiotherapy centre billed sessions on days it was closed.

title: Swoop-and-squat crash caused by two cooperating cars
description: One car cut in sharply in front of the insured vehicle while a second car boxed it in from the side, forcing an unavoidable collision. The two drivers claimed not to know each other, but phone records showed repeated calls between them before the crash and both had used the same lawyer before.

title: Paper accident: collision invented with borrowed photos
description: Two friends filed a claim for a crash at a junction, with photos, a sketch and witness statements. No damage was found when the cars were inspected, the photos were downloaded from an online forum, and mobile tower data placed both drivers in different cities at the claimed time.

title: Burglary staged to claim jewellery that was never owned
description: The household reported a break-in and listed gold jewellery and electronics worth several lakh rupees. The window had been broken from the inside, purchase invoices were generated on the same day by a single shop, and the neighbours heard nothing although a dog was kept in the yard.

title: Slow pipe leak reported as a sudden burst
description: The claim described a pipe bursting overnight and flooding the flat, ruining flooring and furniture. The plumber's report and mould growth showed water had seeped for many months, which the policy excludes; the earlier complaints to the housing society about damp walls had been left out.

title: Policy bought after the loss had already happened
description: Insurance was taken online late at night, and a claim for flood damage to the car was filed two days later. Weather records, garage intake logs and a photo's metadata showed the car was already under water before the policy was issued; the proposal form answered no to existing damage.

title: Car abandoned and torched to escape loan payments
description: An owner behind on EMI payments reported his hatchback stolen, and it was found burnt out at a quarry a week later. The keys were never handed over, the fuel tank had been drained beforehand, and the car had been advertised for sale at a price far below the outstanding loan.

title: Forged pharmacy and diagnostic bills added to a genuine stay
description: The patient's three-day hospital stay was real, but the claim added MRI scans, specialist visits and expensive injections that the hospital never provided. The extra bills came from a lab that had closed, used invalid GST numbers, and were all printed on the same printer as the claimant's office.

title: Same phone reported lost to several insurers
description: A premium smartphone was declared lost on a train and claimed under three gadget policies taken out within a month of each other. The handset's IMEI was still active on the claimant's own SIM, and each police complaint copy had a different station seal.

title: Two-wheeler fall staged to claim hospital and repair costs
description: The rider said his motorbike skidded on gravel near a construction site, causing a fractured wrist and engine damage. The X-ray belonged to an older injury, the scratches on the bike were made with a tool, and a CCTV camera at the site showed no accident that evening.
